aim_summary.goal: Add one cylindrical pin in the bearing area so the part can rotate around it.
preserve_targets: bearing area and all other non-targeted geometry of the part
aim_summary.expected_outcome: One cylindrical pin is coaxially positioned in the aligned clevis pin holes and provides an axis for rotation while the original part geometry remains unchanged.

operations_plan.summary: Create one separate cylindrical pin coaxial with the aligned clevis pin holes in the clevis mounting end.

steps.description: Create a separate cylindrical pin on the common axis of bore faces FACE 0 and FACE 1.

expected_result.geometry: Exactly one separate cylindrical pin is coaxial with the aligned clevis pin holes F002 in section R01.
expected_result.function: The pin provides a rotational axis at the clevis mounting end.
expected_result.behavior: With a compatible diameter and clearance, the part can rotate around the pin.

validation_criteria.description: Exactly one cylindrical pin exists on the common axis of FACE 0 and FACE 1 in the clevis mounting end.
The pin diameter and length are explicitly resolved and validated against the aligned clevis pin holes before execution.
The pin provides a rotational axis for the part at the bearing area.
The resolved pin-to-hole fit provides sufficient clearance for the part to rotate around the pin.
SOLID 0, including R01, R02, R03, and the existing bearing-hole geometry, remains unchanged by creation of the separate pin.
